decisions.reason: Because it is an incremental improvement to the firm's core infrared heating technology, the firm can use existing engineering and service knowledge to refine it, though limited public prominence leaves some discontinuation risk.
As a core product with its own page and strong overlap with the firm's established gas-infrared expertise, it is easy for management to evaluate and improve, so drop risk is low.
It fits the firm's related heating knowledge base, but as a less prominently shown variant in a narrow portfolio it faces a somewhat higher risk if market learning has been weaker.
Tube heaters are close to the firm's core applications for halls and industrial buildings, so absorptive capacity supports keeping it, although modest visibility suggests some pruning risk.

A standard plaque heater still fits the firm's core capabilities and helps cover price-sensitive customer needs, but overlap with other plaque-heater variants raises a moderate portfolio-rationalisation risk.
Despite strong technical relatedness to the existing offer, its lower visibility and likely overlap with other tube-heater variants make it the most plausible candidate for discontinuation.
